meta.titre: Syllables and Sounds: counting beats and matching vowel sounds
meta.sous_theme: Syllable counting and vowel sounds in the listening section
tags: O Level English - syllables and sounds

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: In the listening section of Paper 1, the examiner reads a passage aloud and later asks about one word that you heard. You might have to say how many syllables it has or which other word has the same sound as a part of it. In a community hall in Bamenda, a choir teacher claps the beats of a song so that everyone sings together; you will do the same with words. The key idea is that English spelling does not always match the sound, so you must trust your ears and not your eyes.

items: Vowel letters are a, e, i, o and u; the other letters are consonants.
Words are made of sounds, and a sound is not always one letter.
Two words rhyme when they end with the same sound (*light* and *night*).

sections.contenu_markdown:
### What is a syllable?

A syllable is a beat in a word, and each syllable has **one vowel sound**. Count the vowel *sounds*, not the vowel letters. Say the word slowly and clap each beat.

| Word | Syllables | Split |
|---|---|---|
| make | 1 | make |
| table | 2 | ta-ble |
| guidelines | 2 | guide-lines |
| umbrella | 3 | um-brel-la |
| information | 4 | in-for-ma-tion |
| examination | 5 | ex-am-i-na-tion |

A final silent *e* does not make a syllable (*make*, *guide*, *lines*). The ending *-tion* is one syllable.

### The ending -ed

The ending *-ed* has three sounds, decided by the last sound before it.

- **/t/** after voiceless sounds such as p, k, f, s, sh, ch: *stopped, walked, laughed, missed, washed, watched*.
- **/d/** after voiced sounds: *played, called, lived, begged*.
- **/ɪd/** after t or d: *wanted, needed, accepted, decided*. Only this form adds a syllable (*wanted* has two syllables, *walked* has one).

### The ending -s or -es

- **/s/** after p, t, k, f: *cats, books, cups*.
- **/z/** after voiced sounds and vowels: *dogs, bags, boys, bells*.
- **/ɪz/** after s, z, sh, ch, j sounds: *buses, boxes, dishes, churches, judges*. This form adds a syllable.

### Same spelling, different sounds

The letters *ea* are pronounced in several ways: *eat* and *team* (long ee), *head* and *bread* (short e), *break* and *great* (long a), *ear* and *fears* (ear), *bear* and *pear* (air). The letters *ough* are also irregular: *though* rhymes with *go*, *through* with *too*, *rough* and *enough* with *stuff*, *cough* with *off*.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question asks which word has as many syllables as a heard word
variantes.contenu_markdown: Split the heard word into beats, count them, then split every option in the same way. Choose the option with the same count. Do not count letters or vowel letters.

variantes.nom: Same sound as the underlined part
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question underlines letters in a heard word
variantes.contenu_markdown: Say the heard word and keep only the underlined sound in your head. Say each option and find the one that has the same sound in the same part of the word. A different spelling with the same sound is the right answer; the same spelling with a different sound is a trap.

sections.enonce_markdown:
The listening passage contained the word "beautiful". Choose the option with as many syllables as "beautiful".

A) police   B) umbrella   C) community   D) hand

etapes.action: Say the heard word slowly and clap the beats.
etapes.justification: A syllable is a beat with one vowel sound.
"Beautiful" has five vowel letters (e, a, u, i, u) but only three vowel sounds.
Use the same slow, clapped reading for each word.
etapes.resultat_markdown: police = po-lice (2); umbrella = um-brel-la (3); community = com-mu-ni-ty (4); hand = hand (1).

etapes.justification: Only one option has three beats.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The correct answer is **B) umbrella**, which has three syllables like "beautiful".

items.erreur_markdown: "Guidelines has five vowel letters (u, i, e, i, e), so it has five syllables."
items.pourquoi_faux: Syllables are counted by vowel sounds, and silent letters give none.

items.erreur_markdown: "Make has two syllables because it ends with e."
items.pourquoi_faux: A final silent e is not pronounced and adds no beat.
After /k/, the ending is pronounced /t/ and is joined to the word. Only /ɪd/ (after t or d) adds a syllable.

items.erreur_markdown: "Hear and bear have the same sound in *ea* because they are spelt in the same way."
items.pourquoi_faux: The same spelling can stand for different sounds; *hear* has the ear sound and *bear* has the air sound.

items.erreur_markdown: "Cough and though rhyme because both end in -ough."
items.pourquoi_faux: The letters *ough* have several sounds in English.

items.enonce_markdown:
Give the number of syllables of each word.

(a) banana

(b) table

(c) important

(d) information

(e) walked
items.solution_markdown:
(a) ba-na-na: **3**.

(b) ta-ble: **2**.

(c) im-por-tant: **3**.

(d) in-for-ma-tion: **4** (*-tion* is one beat).

(e) walked: **1** (the ending is /t/).

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Put each word in the correct group according to the sound of its ending: /t/, /d/ or /ɪd/.

watched, called, needed, stopped, decided, lived

(b) Which word has the same ending sound as the s of "buses"?

A) cats   B) dogs   C) churches   D) books
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **/t/:** watched, stopped. **/d/:** called, lived. **/ɪd/:** needed, decided. After t or d the ending is /ɪd/; after a voiceless sound (ch, p) it is /t/; after a voiced sound (l, v) it is /d/.

(b) **C) churches.** The s of *buses* is pronounced /ɪz/, and the same sound ends *churches* (after the ch sound). *Cats* and *books* end in /s/; *dogs* ends in /z/.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) Choose the word whose underlined letters *ea* have a different sound from the other three: bread, head, dead, beach.

(b) Choose the word whose underlined letters *ea* have a different sound from the other three: wear, bear, pear, hear.

(c) You hear the sentence "Tears ran down her face." Which word has the same *ea* sound as the first word? A) bears   B) wears   C) fears   D) pears

(d) Which word rhymes with "enough"? A) though   B) through   C) rough   D) bought

(e) How many syllables are there in "examination" and in "community"?
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **beach.** It has the long ee sound; the other three have the short e sound.

(b) **hear.** It has the ear sound; the other three have the air sound.

(c) **C) fears.** Here *tears* means drops from the eyes and sounds like *ears*; *fears* has the same sound. *Bears, wears* and *pears* have the air sound.

(d) **C) rough.** Both words end in the sound of *stuff*.

(e) **examination = 5** (ex-am-i-na-tion); **community = 4** (com-mu-ni-ty).

items_markdown: A syllable is one beat with one vowel sound: count sounds, not letters.
A silent final e adds no syllable, and *-tion* is one syllable.
The ending *-ed* is /t/, /d/ or /ɪd/; only /ɪd/ (after t or d) adds a syllable.
The ending *-s/-es* is /s/, /z/ or /ɪz/; only /ɪz/ adds a syllable.
The same letters can have different sounds (*ea*, *ough*), so compare sounds by rhyming words, never by spelling.
